title: Hip fracture: initial, subsequent or history
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's hip fracture at this visit.
note:
Chief Complaint
Persistent pain in the right hip.

HPI
The patient is a 79-year-old female presenting today for evaluation of chronic discomfort localized to the right hip. She reports that the pain is most significant when she attempts to stand from a seated position or when walking long distances. She describes the sensation as a dull ache that occasionally sharpens with weight-bearing. She notes that she has had a history of a hip fracture involving the right femoral neck several years ago. She clarifies that the site of the previous hip fracture is completely healed and she requires no further treatment for that specific injury. She is seeking management for the current localized discomfort which is distinct from her previous injury.

Review of Systems
The patient denies fever, chills, or recent weight loss. She denies any shortness of breath, chest pain, or palpitations. She denies any recent falls or new onset of numbness or tingling in her lower extremities. She denies any changes in bowel or bladder habits.

Social History
The patient lives at home with her spouse. She is retired and enjoys gardening and walking in her neighborhood. She denies tobacco use and reports social alcohol consumption on weekends.

Family History
Mother had hypertension and type 2 diabetes. Father had a history of coronary artery disease.

Vitals
Temperature: 98.6 F
Blood Pressure: 132/84 mmHg
Heart Rate: 72 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
SpO2: 98% on room air
Weight: 155 lbs

Recent Labs
Hemoglobin: 12.4 g/dL
White Blood Cell Count: 7.2 x 10^9/L
Glucose: 108 mg/dL
eGFR: 68 mL/min/1.73m2

Medication List
Lisinopril 10 mg daily
Atorvastatin 20 mg daily
Multivitamin daily

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. She appears in no acute distress. Physical examination of the right hip reveals mild tenderness to palpation over the joint line. Range of motion is slightly limited by discomfort but remains stable. No erythema or warmth is noted. Strength is 5/5 in the lower extremities. Gait is steady with a slight limp on the right side.

Assessment
1. Chronic pain of the right hip.
2. History of right femoral neck fracture, completely healed.

Plan
The patient will begin a regimen of acetaminophen 650 mg every 6 hours as needed for pain. We discussed activity modification to avoid overexertion of the right hip. She will return in four weeks for a follow-up to assess the effectiveness of the current pain management strategy.

Electronically signed,
D. Kowalski, NP
May 14, 2026
explanations: A hip fracture that has completely healed, with treatment finished: personal history, Z87.81 (no HCC).

distractors.why: The fracture has healed and needs no more care: Z87.81.
The fracture has healed; an initial-encounter code would add HCC 402.
